key_insight: A scalable causal Bayesian network framework can turn large EHR datasets into interpretable cancer prescreening models with evidence paths that are easier to inspect than standard black-box ML.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help support earlier cancer risk flagging in EHR settings while making model reasoning more transparent for research and workflow review.
method: Adaptive data slicing to split large EHR data for parallel learning
Quality-aware structure aggregation to combine learned networks
Global DAG construction to produce a stable causal-interpretable Bayesian network
evidence_signal: In simulations, the method improved structural recovery by nearly 40% and sped up learning by up to 221.28-fold; in EHR prescreening it achieved AUCs of 0.8171 for esophageal cancer and 0.784 for colorectal cancer.
watch_item: As with observational EHR modeling, learned causal directions are putative rather than proven, so external validation and careful implementation are important.
paper_title: Scalable Causal-Interpretable Machine Learning for Cancer Prescreening Using Electronic Health Records
